subject: Arrays, vectors and matrices: slicing and efficiency

messages.author: abab84dd2ba42997
messages.subject: Arrays, vectors and matrices: slicing and efficiency
parts:
Hi ever-helpful Stan list,

I'm trying to get my head around the relative efficiencies of arrays, vectors and matrices. As I understand it from the manual, if your model can do pure linear algebra then it's best to use matrices / vectors as appropriate, but if you need to index individual scalars then arrays are faster (with row-wise indexing)?

For example, in the attached model, parameter z is declared as a matrix:

matrix<lower=0>[SF,S] z;




then later in the model block, z is indexed like so:

pow(z[targ_sf,subj],p[subj])




where targ_sf and subj are integers.

Would it be faster in this case to declare z as an array, like so?

real<lower=0> z[SF, S];



Any other efficiency suggestions in the attached model would also be appreciated (I understand that binomial rather than bernoulli would be much faster but that's unfortunately not possible here).

Thanks in advance.

Tom

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Arrays, vectors and matrices: slicing and efficiency
parts:
On 11/6/13, 10:03 AM, Tom Wallis wrote:
> Hi ever-helpful Stan list,
>
> I'm trying to get my head around the relative efficiencies of arrays, vectors and matrices. As I understand it from the
> manual,

You read the new manual chapter? I was trying to make that
self contained. When I get some time, I'll make sure to discuss
binary indexing in 2D arrays vs. matrices.

> if your model can do pure linear algebra then it's best to use matrices / vectors as appropriate, but if you
> need to index individual scalars then arrays are faster (with row-wise indexing)?
You need to use matrices or vectors to do linear algebra.

> For example, in the attached model, parameter z is declared as a matrix:
>
> |
> matrix<lower=0>[SF,S] z;
>
>
> |
>
>
> then later in the model block, z is indexed like so:
>
> |
> pow(z[targ_sf,subj],p[subj])
>
>
> |
>
>
> where targ_sf and subj are integers.
>
> Would it be faster in this case to declare z as an array, like so?
>
> |
> real<lower=0> z[SF, S];

No matrices are faster for binary indexing. But really I don't think
it'll be a big enough effect to notice.

An array of row vectors is fastest for pulling out whole rows.

>
> Any other efficiency suggestions in the attached model would also be appreciated (I understand that binomial rather than
> bernoulli would be much faster but that's unfortunately not possible here).

The biggest improvements come from vectorization. So turn these:

for (i in 1:SF){
z[i] ~ lognormal(log(z_mu[i]),0.5);
w[i] ~ cauchy(w_mu[i],1);
}


into

z ~ lognormal(log(z_mu), 0.5);
w ~ cauchy(w_mu,1);


But you've already done that in the main Bernoulli likelihood,
so that may dominate the computation time.

A deeper change would be to use inv_logit rather than Phi
or the approximate Phi --- the cumulative normal's a very
expensive function to evaluate. Evaluating Phi is going to
dwarf the difference between array and matrix lookup.

- Bob
